content.text:
I fixed the bug in `src/parser/parser.ts`. Your example now loads to `{ a: { oneOf: [ { type: 'string', example: '\n' }, { type: 'array' } ] } }`, the same result as 4.3.2.

**Cause:** in `readBlockScalar`, the parser records how far the leading blank lines are indented. When it reached the first line with real text, it threw "bad indentation of a mapping entry" if that line was less indented than those blank lines. That check is right when the line belongs to the scalar: per the YAML spec, leading blank lines can't be indented more than the first content line. But it also fired on lines that end the scalar, like `    - type: array` or a sibling key. So a whitespace-only body followed by a less indented line was wrongly rejected.

**Fix** (`src/parser/parser.ts:712`): the check now applies only when the line is indented enough to be part of the scalar's content. Any less indented line ends the scalar, as it already did when the blank line had no spaces.

**Results:**
- `|+` and `>+` give `"\n"`; `|`, `>` and `|-` give `""`.
- The sibling-key case `a:\n  x: |+\n      \n  y: 1\n` gives `{ a: { x: '\n', y: 1 } }`.
- Input that really is invalid, such as `a: |\n     \n  x\n`, still raises the error.

I added regression tests for these cases in `test/core/units/load-other.test.mjs`. After a rebuild, the core suite passes: 315 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped. I couldn't run the yaml-test-suite spec tests because their fixtures have to be downloaded (`npm run spec:get`), which needs the network.

I fixed the bug in `src/parser/parser.ts`. Your example now loads to `{ a: { oneOf: [ { type: 'string', example: '\n' }, { type: 'array' } ] } }`, the same result as 4.3.2.

**Cause:** in `readBlockScalar`, the parser records how far the leading blank lines are indented. When it reached the first line with real text, it threw "bad indentation of a mapping entry" if that line was less indented than those blank lines. That check is right when the line belongs to the scalar: per the YAML spec, leading blank lines can't be indented more than the first content line. But it also fired on lines that end the scalar, like `    - type: array` or a sibling key. So a whitespace-only body followed by a less indented line was wrongly rejected.

**Fix** (`src/parser/parser.ts:712`): the check now applies only when the line is indented enough to be part of the scalar's content. Any less indented line ends the scalar, as it already did when the blank line had no spaces.

**Results:**
- `|+` and `>+` give `"\n"`; `|`, `>` and `|-` give `""`.
- The sibling-key case `a:\n  x: |+\n      \n  y: 1\n` gives `{ a: { x: '\n', y: 1 } }`.
- Input that really is invalid, such as `a: |\n     \n  x\n`, still raises the error.

I added regression tests for these cases in `test/core/units/load-other.test.mjs`. After a rebuild, the core suite passes: 315 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped. I couldn't run the yaml-test-suite spec tests because their fixtures have to be downloaded (`npm run spec:get`), which needs the network.
